title: Year four close: the many rooms
hookLine: thinkers, prayers, ethics, hope and the hardest questions: one house with many rooms (John 14:2)
tomorrow: Four women in the family tree (Matthew 1:1–17)

lines: WE KNOW NOT WHITHER THOU GOEST.
THE SAME LINE, THE SAME ROOM.
cards: At the table on Jesus' last night, one of his friends admits he's lost. Jesus has just told them not to be troubled, and that he is going to prepare a place for them.
Thomas doesn't nod along: "Lord, we know not whither thou goest; and how can we know the way?" This year opened with the promise Thomas was answering, about a house with many rooms.
Today the year closes in the same room, with the same line, and Thomas's question still on the table.

teach.h: MANY MANSIONS: A PLACE FOR YOU.
teach.b: John's Gospel, in the King James: "In my Father's house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you."

teach.h: THE YEAR, ONE ROOM AT A TIME.
teach.b: This year walked that house room by room. The big questions, each church answering in its own voice. Prayer, from the Jesus Prayer to Quaker silence to a hymn.
Ethics: commandments, virtues and mercy. The great thinkers, arguing across the centuries. Revelation and Christian hope, from a garden to a garden-city.
Church life: rites and spaces, bells and bread. And these last weeks, the hardest room: suffering, doubt, grief, and love that walks into pain without explaining it.
Now notice who first heard many mansions. Frightened friends. Peter, just told he would deny Jesus before the rooster crowed.
Thomas, saying out loud that he didn't know the way. Right after Peter hears that, Jesus says: "Let not your heart be troubled." And then: "I go to prepare a place for you."
A place prepared for them as they are: troubled, unsure, about to fail.
Christians read the line in more than one way: some hear it about heaven, some about the church on earth, some about life with God that starts now, and some readers hold those side by side.

teach.h: THE ROOM COMES BEFORE THE ANSWERS.
teach.b: But in the story, the promise of a room comes before the confusion is cleared up. Thomas asks his question, and what he hears next is an answer, not a rebuke.

how: John 14 is read at some Christian funerals, and some churches return to these chapters of Jesus' last night during Holy Week.

o: a final exam on everything taught across the year
the end of the whole path, with nothing after it
the last day of a year spent in one house of many rooms

s: Jesus spoke of many mansions at a celebration after Easter
he said it on his last night, at the table, to friends who were troubled.
Thomas answers the promise of a place with a question
"Lord, we know not whither thou goest; and how can we know the way?"
this year set out to decide which church has the right answers
it walked through the house one room at a time and let each church answer in its own voice.

games.q: you're Thomas, at the table. Jesus has just said he's going to prepare a place for you, and that you know the way. you don't. what do you do?
o: say plainly that you don't know where he's going.
games.why: Thomas says: Lord, we know not whither thou goest; and how can we know the way? and what he gets back is an answer, not a rebuke.

practice: Walk back through the year's rooms in your mind and notice which one you kept returning to and which one you're standing in today. It might be the room of doubt, with Thomas; that's a room in the house, too.
Let one line form, I live in the room of, and finish it yourself; if you pray, offer it to God as it is.

wordCard.voice: Year four close. The last day of a year spent in one house with many rooms: thinkers, prayer, ethics, hope and the hardest questions. A house first promised to friends who were afraid.

orig.note: Greek: a dwelling place, a room to stay in. the word behind many mansions in John 14:2.
